items.title: China tests microwave beam to recharge drones midair

featured_image.name: China demonstrates microwave beam that recharges drones in ...

items.description:
Chinese scientists have demonstrated a system that wirelessly transmits power from a ground vehicle to a drone in flight using microwave energy, a development that could one day allow unmanned aircraft to stay airborne indefinitely.

The research, published on March 25 in the peer-reviewed Chinese journal Aeronautical Science & Technology, was carried out by a team from Xidian University, an institution known for its military technology work, according to the South China Morning Post. The system uses a car-mounted microwave emitter to beam energy to an antenna array fitted to the drone's underside — and critically, it works while both the vehicle and the aircraft are moving.[1]

items.title: UAE asks U.S. for dollar swap line as Iran war strains economy

featured_image.name: Iran war wipes $120bn off Dubai, Abu Dhabi stock markets

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates has quietly initiated discussions with the United States about a potential financial safety net as the war with Iran continues to strain its economy, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal on Saturday.[1][2]

UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the idea of a dollar currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve officials during meetings in Washington last week, where the Central Bank of the UAE was participating in the IMF and World Bank spring meetings. U.S. officials described the overture as precautionary rather than a formal request, with Emirati representatives stressing that they have so far managed to avoid the worst economic consequences of the conflict but may still need a backstop.[3][1]

items.title: Exit polls show Radev winning Bulgaria election by wide margin
items.description:
Former Bulgarian President Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria coalition is on track to win Sunday's parliamentary election by a commanding margin, exit polls showed, raising hopes of ending years of political chaos in the Balkan nation but also stoking concern over a potential shift in the country's stance toward Russia and Ukraine.

Exit surveys by the Trend research group projected Radev's center-left coalition at roughly 39% of the vote, more than double the share of his closest rival, the center-right GERB party led by longtime Prime Minister Boyko Borissov, which polled at about 15%. A separate Alpha Research exit poll broadly confirmed the result. Six parties are expected to clear the 4% threshold needed to enter the 240-seat National Assembly.[1][2][3]
